title: DOJ Withheld 53 Pages of Epstein Files Naming Trump Including FBI 302s
description_short: DOJ Withheld 53 Pages of Epstein Files Naming Trump Including FBI 302s
description_medium: The DOJ withheld 53 pages of Epstein files mentioning Trump from initial releases, including three FBI FD-302 interview summaries from 2019 regarding an allegation that Trump sexually assaulted a 13-to-15-year-old circa 1983. Released March 5, 2026 after an NPR investigation revealed missing documents. As of March 2026, 37 pages remained missing. Deputy AG Todd Blanche stated We did not protect President Trump in the releases but was criticized for delaying release.
description_long: NPR reported that the Justice Department initially left out 53 pages of Epstein-related records mentioning Donald Trump. The documents included three FBI FD-302 interview summaries from 2019 concerning a woman’s allegation that Trump sexually assaulted her when she was 13 to 15, around 1983. An FD-302 records an interview; the existence of those summaries does not establish that the alleged assault occurred. After NPR reported the omissions, the department released the pages on March 5, 2026, while 37 pages still had not been released as of that month. Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche said the department had not protected Trump in its releases, amid criticism over the delay. The disclosure dispute is distinct from the underlying allegation: the account documents which records were initially withheld, which were later published, and what remained missing. It does not report a finding about the allegation or explain why each page was withheld.

description_short: A FBI spokesperson confirms the girlfriend of FBI director Kash Patel had a protective detail of FBI SWAT team members due to reported threats against her
description_medium: An FBI spokesperson confirmed on Nov. 17, 2025, that FBI Director Kash Patel’s girlfriend had a protective detail staffed by FBI SWAT members after reported threats against her. The supplied account identifies the protection and its stated reason, but does not describe the threats, the detail’s scope, or its duration.

title: 238 Venezuelans Mass-Deported to CECOT Using Tattoo 'Gang Points System'
description_short: 238 Venezuelans Mass-Deported to CECOT Using Tattoo 'Gang Points System'
description_medium: On March 15, 2025, the Trump administration sent 238 Venezuelan men to El Salvador’s CECOT prison under the Alien Enemies Act. ProPublica reported that nearly half had active immigration cases and that officials used a tattoo-based points system to classify alleged gang ties. The transfer occurred without individual due-process hearings, according to the supplied account.
description_long: On March 15, 2025, the Trump administration invoked the 1798 Alien Enemies Act to send 238 Venezuelan men to El Salvador’s CECOT prison without individual immigration hearings, according to the supplied account. ProPublica reported that 118 of the men had active immigration cases when they were deported. Its reporting described a government points system that treated tattoos, including roses, crowns and family names, as indicators of gang membership. The system’s use made personal appearance and tattoos part of the basis for labeling people as gang-linked, even as pending cases meant many men still had immigration proceedings underway. One case highlighted was Andry Hernández, a gay barber whose wrist tattoos reading “mom” and “dad,” accompanied by crowns, were assigned five points. The account says he was photographed kneeling in chains while guards slapped him. Those details describe the reporting’s account of how the removals were carried out; the material supplied here does not include individual case files or the government’s explanation for each designation. The episode raised a due-process issue because people were transferred to a foreign prison without case-by-case hearings while many immigration cases remained active.

title: Mar-a-Lago Used as Classified Situation Room While Paying Members Mingle
description_short: Mar-a-Lago Used as Classified Situation Room While Paying Members Mingle
description_medium: Throughout 2025–2026, Trump repeatedly directed classified military operations from Mar-a-Lago — including the opening of the Houthi air campaign (March 2025), Christmas Day Tomahawk strikes in Nigeria, and the Iran bombing campaign (February 2026) — while hundreds of paying club members and their guests attended events on the same grounds. Intelligence professionals warned the arrangement created serious counterintelligence vulnerabilities. No protocols exist for screening club visitors against classified materials.
description_long: CNN reported that President Donald Trump monitored the January 2026 operation to capture Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro from a secured viewing area at Mar-a-Lago. Black drapes created the viewing space in the club’s Tea Room, with secure internet, a dedicated telephone system and monitors carrying real-time information. The operation was underway while ordinary club activity continued: members and guests arrived, although the report said the viewing setup was placed away from them. CNN described the overlap between a private club and high-level national-security work as a longstanding concern for intelligence officials. The Secret Service screens people entering the property but does not control access to the club itself, according to the report. CNN also recounted an earlier episode in which guests could hear Trump and Japan’s prime minister discuss a response to a North Korean missile launch and post photos online. The January operation illustrates the security and confidentiality questions raised when presidential military decisions are handled at a commercial club. The linked article does not support the separate Houthi, Nigeria and Iran examples in the preserved medium description.

title: EPA Proposes Repealing Endangerment Finding — Legal Basis for All Climate Rules
description_short: EPA Proposes Repealing Endangerment Finding — Legal Basis for All Climate Rules
description_medium: On July 29, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced a proposal to repeal the 2009 endangerment finding, the agency’s scientific determination that greenhouse-gas emissions threaten public health. EPA said it no longer reflected current science, economics or law and estimated repeal would save $54 billion annually. The action was a proposal, not a completed repeal.
description_long: On July 29, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced a proposal to rescind the agency’s 2009 endangerment finding. That finding concluded that greenhouse-gas emissions endanger public health and welfare, and it has served as a central basis for federal climate regulation. Zeldin argued that the determination no longer reflected current science, economics or law. The EPA estimated that ending the finding would save $54 billion a year by eliminating climate standards. Because the agency announced a proposal, the July action began a process rather than immediately removing the finding or cancelling existing limits. The proposal put vehicle-emissions rules and other greenhouse-gas standards at issue, but the supplied material does not show the final rule’s terms or the status of each regulation. Describing the announcement as an automatic repeal of every climate rule would overstate what had occurred at that point. Its immediate significance was the administration’s attempt to undo the scientific and legal foundation used for federal greenhouse-gas regulation, with the practical reach dependent on the final agency action and any legal challenges.

preserved_fields.title: EPA Proposes Repealing Endangerment Finding — Legal Basis for All Climate Rules
preserved_fields.description_short: EPA Proposes Repealing Endangerment Finding — Legal Basis for All Climate Rules

notes: The entry describes a proposal. The supplied reporting does not establish that existing standards had already been revoked or that all climate rules would automatically become void.
